perspective:
From Christian Mensah’s subjective perspective, he has access to the following information:

- He is a Black male police officer and knows Jonathan is his childhood best friend, an African American carpenter with a master’s degree. He often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- Lately, Christian felt Jonathan was acting differently and hiding something important. He became anxious and suspicious, and arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop.
- At that meeting, Christian told Jonathan he needed to talk seriously and felt Jonathan was hiding something. He heard Jonathan say he could trust him. When pressed, Jonathan admitted he had kept something from Christian: Jonathan is in trouble and did not know how to tell him.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He offered help, saying they could face it together. Jonathan said the situation was complicated and he did not want to drag Christian into it. Christian insisted as his best friend. Jonathan said he could use support and resources, and needed to figure a way out.
- Christian came to believe Jonathan’s trouble might involve criminal activity. He asked if it was illegal. Jonathan said he could not say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself. Christian said he would look into it discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his investigation, Christian concluded that Jonathan was being framed and that someone was trying to set him up. He told Jonathan this. Jonathan asked if he was sure and who would do that. Christian said he was not sure yet but had leads and would gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence. Jonathan thanked him.
- Christian later found out/believed the real culprit was someone close to both him and Jonathan, someone they both knew and trusted. He told Jonathan he had found out who was behind it and that it was someone they both knew and trusted, though he did not name the person in the exchange. Christian felt betrayed and resolved to confront the culprit and bring them to justice. Jonathan warned him the person was dangerous but said he trusted Christian.
- Christian decided to confront the real culprit and ensure justice was done.

He does not have access to hidden events, Jonathan’s private thoughts, or facts neither observed, heard, told to him, nor discovered through his own investigation.
